description:
## Problem
Nothing shows who holds the host lock, who waits, what VMs reserve memory, or which orphaned servers are still running. Agents start servers by hand outside every entry point: two native QuestDB JVMs orphaned to launchd (one with `-XX:+AlwaysPreTouch`, one at 2.3 GB RSS) run from BenchBox worktrees, and no repo code launches them. Without a rule, agents keep doing this.

## Change
1. `python -m benchbox.utils.host_lock status` and `make heavy-status`: holder record and age, live waiter count, admission readings (pressure, memorystatus_level, available memory, VM reservations, free disk), top 10 processes by physical footprint, and orphaned JVMs/servers (ppid 1 with cwd inside a BenchBox worktree). Read-only.
2. `make heavy-run CMD="..."` wrapping `python -m benchbox.utils.host_lock run -- sh -c "$(CMD)"` for ad-hoc heavy work.
3. AGENTS.md rule `[HEAVY-LOCK-001]` (compact, linked to a detail doc under docs/agent/): heavy work runs only through entry points that take the lock or through `make heavy-run`; hand-started servers run under `make heavy-run` and are stopped afterwards; never move, delete or recreate the lock file; never set `BENCHBOX_SKIP_TEST_LOCK`, `BENCHBOX_HEAVY_ADMIT=force` or `BENCHBOX_HEAVY_WATCHDOG=off` without the owner's approval in the current task; check `make heavy-status` before starting heavy work.
4. Record a deferral for the optional rename (`test.lock` -> `heavy.lock`, `BENCHBOX_TEST_LOCK_*` -> `BENCHBOX_HEAVY_LOCK_*`).

## Decision gates
- G1 (stop condition): AGENTS.md is the compact authority; if the rule needs more than ~6 lines there, put detail in `docs/agent/heavy-work.md` and link it.
- G2: status must not require the lock and must finish in under 5 s even when the `container` CLI hangs (per-command timeouts).

## Guardrails
- Status never signals or modifies processes, VMs or the lock file.
- Linked worktree; stage explicitly; `[COMMENT-POLICY-001]`; docs/agent stays unpublished (not in docs/publish-allowlist.txt).

## Non-goals
Killing orphans automatically.
